svg.text: Clean Agent & Kitchen Suppression — No Residue, No Damage, Right Chemistry
Halon 1301 was the original clean agent — banned by the Montreal Protocol for ozone depletion. Modern replacements are governed by NFPA 2001.
FM-200 (HFC-227ea)
Suppresses fire by absorbing heat from
combustion. Class A, B, C hazards.
Design concentration: ~7-8%
Zero ozone depletion — significant global
warming potential.
Fluorinated ketone, suppresses by
absorbing heat — similar design concentration.
Zero ODP, very low GWP
Both agents safe for occupied spaces at
design concentration when properly engineered.
Wet chemical kitchen hood suppression — NFPA 17A
Potassium-based agent saponifies hot cooking oils into a soapy foam — the reaction cools the oil and
seals the surface against oxygen, preventing re-ignition after knockdown.
K-class portable extinguishers required nearby
Commercial cooking equipment only — a different chemistry problem than total-flooding clean agents.
NFPA 2001 governs clean agent total-flooding systems; NFPA 17A governs wet chemical kitchen
suppression — two different standards, two different agents.
